_doc: Megaflora — the big things. The ask was 'give another pass over each biome and add large objects … giant trees, boulders, arches, or other features. They should be 2-3 times taller than our tallest trees currently.' The tallest ordinary prop in js/props.js is the conifer at 9 metres, so everything here stands between 17 and 26 — two to three times that — and every land biome gets at least one. They are rolled on their OWN random stream (see the `0x4d67` salt in props.js) so that adding them did not reshuffle a single tree that was already there.
_harvestDoc:
R17 — A MEGA-TREE YOU CAN ACTUALLY CUT DOWN.

"I found one of the new mega-trees at (seed 56138, Chodikvraun III, biome Grassland, x 11438, z 3187, altitude 22) but was disappointed I could not cut it down. Could these trees be updated to be cut down and reward ~15 times more than a normal tree? Obviously this should only work for mega trees actually made of wood, but maybe not all mega-structures."

He could not, and the reason is the same shape as everything else this round: js/props.js keeps a harvest ledger (`felled`, by `propKey`, saved) and a `standing` list of everything you can walk up to and hit — and megaflora were never put on either. They are drawn out of their own `megaMeshes` on their own random stream, and the line that files an ordinary tree as hittable (`if (PROP_HARVEST[key]) standing.push(...)`) is in the ordinary prop loop, two hundred lines above the giant one. So a 24 m tree was scenery with a collision cylinder round it. Nothing was broken; the join had never been made.

WHICH ONES. `wood: true` is an EXPLICIT flag rather than a guess at the name, because 'hollow_snag' and 'crown_conifer' share no word and 'crystal_spire' and 'shelf_palm' both end in a plant. Only the four wood-bodied kinds can be felled. Everything else carries `why`, a sentence the game says when you swing at it, because a giant that refuses silently reads exactly like the bug being fixed here.

WHAT IT PAYS. Fifteen times the ordinary tree of the same family, to the log: a broadleaf drops 9 logs, an Elder Broadleaf drops 135. `tier` is one step above its ordinary cousin (a Crown Conifer needs steel where a pine needs iron) and `seconds` is the gather bar — four to seven times a normal tree — so the payout is earned rather than collected. `regrow` is deliberately far longer than the 6 hours an ordinary tree takes: a giant is a landmark, and one that grew back over lunch would stop being one.

_schema.kinds: the catalogue. `tall` is roughly how high it stands (the test checks it against the tallest ordinary tree), `solid` is [radius, height] for the collision field — carried here rather than in js/collide.js's PROP_SOLIDS because that file belongs to somebody else this round, `leafy` says the biome's leaf tint applies. `wood` says it can be felled; a wood kind carries `harvest` and a non-wood one carries `why`.
_schema.harvest: { like: the ordinary PROP_HARVEST row this is fifteen of, tier: the tool tier the swing must clear, hp: how much damage brings it down if you insist on hitting it with a sword, seconds: the gather bar, drops: what it leaves before the per-instance size scaling, verb, work: which mining clip the body plays, regrow: in-game seconds }
_schema.biomes: [[kind, chance per 64 m prop cell at density 1]] — a chance of 0.02 is about four in the block of ground you can see, which is rare enough that each one still reads as a place.
_schema.minSlope: steeper than this and nothing this big would have stayed up
_schema.roadClear: how much road under a point rules it out — nobody lets a 24 m tree grow through the highway

tor.name: Tor
tor.why: A tor is the hill with the soil washed off it. There is no felling that.

stone_arch.name: Stone Arch
stone_arch.why: The arch is one piece of bedrock. Take a bite out of it and the rest comes down on you.

basalt_stack.name: Basalt Stack
basalt_stack.why: Cooled lava, in columns, all the way through. Quarry it properly or leave it alone.

crystal_spire.name: Crystal Spire
crystal_spire.why: It is a single crystal twenty-five metres tall. Nothing you are carrying will start it.

ice_fang.name: Ice Fang
ice_fang.why: Ice this old is rock. A tool made for wood only polishes it.

cap_mushroom.name: Cap Mushroom
cap_mushroom.why: The stalk is wet pulp — it tears rather than cuts, and nothing useful comes off it.

rib_arch.name: Rib Arch
rib_arch.why: Whatever it was the bones of, they went to stone a long time ago.

mast_cactus.name: Mast Cactus
mast_cactus.why: Under the spines it is all water and pith. There is no timber in a cactus.
